description: Open redirect in a login redirect or 'next' parameter. After authentication the application redirects the user to a URL supplied in a GET/POST parameter (e.g. ?next=, ?redirect=, ?url=) without validating that the destination is on the same domain. An attacker can craft a phishing link that sends victims to an arbitrary external site after a seemingly legitimate login.
exploit_hint: Submit /login?next=https://attacker.example.com. After a successful (or even failed) login, the server should redirect to the arbitrary URL in the 'next' parameter.
requirements: The /login endpoint MUST accept a 'next' (or 'redirect', 'url', 'return') GET parameter.
After processing the login form the server MUST redirect to whatever URL is in that parameter.
The server MUST NOT check that the redirect target is on the same origin or whitelist.
Include a realistic 'Remember where you were going' UX comment in the HTML to explain the parameter's presence.
